summary: NewDataBlob silently ignores invalid encoding type strings by setting ENCODING_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED instead of returning errors to callers, causing encoding failures to only surface later during deserialization.
userImpact: Developers cannot immediately detect encoding type errors when creating data blobs, making it harder to diagnose serialization failures.
rootCause: NewDataBlob catches EncodingTypeFromString errors but silently sets ENCODING_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED instead of returning the error to callers.
proposedFix: Change function signature to return (*commonpb.DataBlob, error) and return error when encoding type is invalid, or create a separate NewDataBlobWithError variant.
